_about: The material rule's weights: the one place they are written. web/landform.js imports this file and bozkir/landform.py reads it, so the viewer, the figures and the validation all use the same numbers. Each class is a position on a hillside. Its score is (1 - altitude) x (the weighted terms below) + altitude x (its height term), where altitude is the viewer's 'follows height'. Terms: drive = drainage (or the erosion's sediment record where there is one), hollow = 1 - topographic position, ridge = topographic position, slope, flat = 1 - slope, midpos = how near the middle of the topographic range. Height: low = 1 - elevation, high = elevation, middle = nearness to mid elevation. Change a number here and both languages follow; tests/test_pipeline.py checks they still agree cell for cell. River rule (classify's river option, off by default): the terms near = 1 - HAND (height above the nearest channel, Renno et al. 2008, along the same D8 receivers as drainage) and channel (cells draining more than river.channel_share of the grid), measured on the height field with its depressions filled (Priority-Flood, as erosion fills); a cell filling raised by more than river.lake_depth of the height range is lake and counts as channel; with the positions edge, bar and bank, from river_classes.
